title: `sort` is stable on the probe, guaranteed only with `maintain_order`
description: Sorting 200 000 rows on a key with 7 values kept the input order within each key, in memory and streaming, with and without `maintain_order`. Polars documents order among ties only for `maintain_order=True`.
`top_k` keeps 2 of 3 tied rows; which ones is not documented.

The streaming sort buffers its input. Up to `POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES` (32 MiB, at most half the out-of-core memory budget) it concatenates the morsels in sequence order and sorts them with the in-memory sort. Above it, it splits the rows into key-range buckets: with `maintain_order` each task reads a contiguous run of frames, which keeps input order within a bucket; without it the frames are dealt to the tasks in turn, and the source does not keep input order among ties. The 200 000-row probe stayed below the threshold. With the threshold lowered to 100 000 bytes, a sort of 200 000 rows on 7 keys still kept input order among ties, with and without `maintain_order`, so the unordered path is unconfirmed.
reference: `tie_order`: any order of the ties, and any rows of a tie for a `fetch`. Every behaviour is allowed.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: below the partition threshold: linearized morsels, in-memory sort
above it: contiguous frame runs per task with `maintain_order`, round-robin without
`partition_frames`: with `maintain_order` a whole frame is stored after the bucket's builder
`DEFAULT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES` 32 MiB, `POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES`, capped at half the budget

200 000 rows, k = i % 7: lf.sort('k', maintain_order=...) kept i increasing within each k, for maintain_order False and True, streaming and in memory, with the default threshold and with POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES=100000 (POLARS_MAX_THREADS=4)
